planting.note: Pot rooted stem or leaf cuttings in spring into fast-draining, gritty cactus mix and site in bright light to full sun, since this jade cultivar is extremely drought-tolerant and rots quickly in wet or dense soil.

directions: ET's Fingers forms the same thick, tubular leaves as the standard jade plant but without the trumpet-like flare at the tip seen on 'Gollum', giving each leaf a straighter, more finger-like profile tipped in red under bright light. Like its relatives, it develops a sturdy, woody, tree-like trunk over time and is a popular subject for succulent bonsai and novelty dish gardens. It shares the jade plant's easy care and drought tolerance, and should be watered only once the soil has dried out fully to avoid root and stem rot. Propagate from stem or leaf cuttings allowed to callus for a day or two before inserting into dry succulent mix.
sources: Cactus and Succulent Society of America reference

common_name: Variegated String of Buttons (Cream-Edged Necklace Vine)

planting.note: Root stem-tip cuttings after the cut end has callused for a few days, then insert into gritty succulent mix and keep barely moist until new growth confirms rooting.

directions: This variegated sport of the common String of Buttons carries the same triangular, stacked leaf pairs threading along trailing stems, but each leaf is broadly margined in cream to pale yellow that often blushes pink in bright light or cool weather. Because the pale leaf tissue carries less chlorophyll, it grows a little more slowly than the solid-green species and benefits from bright but filtered light to prevent scorching along the variegated margins. Grow in a hanging basket or shallow pot of fast-draining succulent mix, letting it dry out fully between waterings, and remove any stems that revert to solid green to keep the variegation strong. Propagate from stem-tip cuttings callused for a few days before inserting into dry succulent mix.
